title: How a Leaf Blower Works in 60 Seconds 🍂💨 #shorts
description:
A leaf blower is a spinning fan in a tube. It sucks air in through a side intake, flings it into the tube, and a narrowing nozzle squeezes it faster. Good yard blowers push over 400 cubic feet of air a minute at over 100 mph, and strong ones top 200 mph. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#leafblower #engineering #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: The strongest leaf blowers shoot air out at over *200 miles per hour*.

steps.label: Motor
steps.text: An engine or electric *motor* spins a small *fan* at very high speed.

steps.label: Intake
steps.text: The spinning blades *suck air in* through a grille on the side.

steps.label: Fling
steps.text: Then they *fling* that air outward, into the long *blower tube*.

steps.label: Nozzle
steps.text: The tube gets *narrower* at the end, so the same air has to move *faster*.

steps.label: Volume
steps.text: Speed lifts leaves, but *volume* pushes them. Good blowers move over *400 cubic feet* a minute.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Suck, fling, *squeeze*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
